messages:
sara (support): heads up — multiple customers reporting 502/504s and a rise in timeouts to the hosted API since the 09:04 canary. stack: api.redwood.com/v1/generate. lots of errors + a billing spike for retries. filing here for triage

alex (eng): seeing the same on dashboards. 5xx rate up ~8x on canary slice, latency P95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.2s. traced a few requests — upstream auth failures then gateway timeouts.

leah (eng-sre): Deploy bot shows canary: enable-prefetch-v2 rolled at 09:04 by jamie. ops-bot posted: "canary roll started: canary/enable-prefetch-v2 (tag: canary-2026-03-17)"

ops-bot: canary deployment: canary/enable-prefetch-v2 started by jamie at 2026-03-17T09:04:12Z

alex (eng): quick grep of logs: lots of entries like:
```
upstream/auth-proxy ERROR "auth header parse failed" host=auth-service request_id=abc123 meta="truncated auth header"
proxy/gateway WARN "upstream returned 502" host=api.redwood.com request_id=abc123
```
Seems the auth header is being normalized differently inside the canary path (suffix stripping) — downstream auth rejects and then client retries piling onto gateway.

maya (infra): reproducer from my laptop (same region):
```
TOKEN=$CUSTOMER_TOKEN
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
# response: 502 Bad Gateway (upstream: 502)
```
If I strip a suffix from the header on the client side it succeeds. suggests canary is mutating header contents.

leah (eng-sre): paging dion (oncall). we need an immediate mitigation: either rollback canary or remove the feature flag for routing to prefetch path. Which can we do faster?

dion (oncall): I can initiate a rollback, but want eng to confirm no DB/schema changes. alex, is this purely request routing / header handling?

alex (eng): yes, only routing/normalizer change in the canary. no schema or model changes. safe to roll back.

jamie (product): confirmed the feature flag toggles a new header-normalizer that strips a trailing auth suffix for older clients. we didn't anticipate tokens with embedded "+" characters — the normalizer was applied unscoped to all traffic in canary slice. my bad.

sara (support): customers to notify: two enterprise customers on canary slice started paging support 09:12. they want ETA and whether keys were rotated.

dion (oncall): rolling back now — running: `orch rollback --deployment canary/enable-prefetch-v2 --to-tag canary-stable-2026-03-16`

ops-bot: rollback job started (id: rb-4242). will update when rollout completes.

leah (eng-sre): I'm throttling canary traffic in the load-balancer to 0% for the affected slice as a precaution while rollback runs. switching traffic -> stable.

maya (infra): rollback finished on control plane side, but edge caches still had a few sticky sessions. invalidating VCL for canary route now.

ops-bot: rollback job rb-4242 succeeded. canary/enable-prefetch-v2 -> rolled back to canary-stable-2026-03-16

alex (eng): monitoring — 5xx rate dropping back toward baseline. P95 back to ~130ms. I see auth failures fall to near-zero after invalidation.

jamie (product): apologies team — I'll open a postmortem. initial notes: unscoped header normalizer applied to canary slice, missed a token edge-case, should have been feature-gated per-client-version.

dion (oncall): customer comms: sara, can you send short note: we rolled back the canary, identified header normalizer as cause, investigating fix and will follow up with timeline. mark as high priority to avoid SLA hits. :thumbsup:

sara (support): sending now. cc: affected customers, CS lead. also asked if they saw billing/credits — finance flagged increased invoice counts due to retries, will evaluate credits after postmortem.

alex (eng): next steps for eng: add tight unit + integration test for auth header variants, create feature-gate that scopes normalizer to client-version, and run a quick canary with 1% traffic and synthetic auth token matrix.

jamie (product): agree. I'll own the rollout checklist updates.

leah (eng-sre): adding runbook note: if auth parse errors spike after deploy, immediate steps: throttle canary -> rollback -> invalidate edge -> confirm 5xx down -> notify customers.

maya (infra): leaving a short repro in case we need it later: header that fails: `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsIn...+abc==` (note the plus sign). normalizer removed characters after "+".

alex (eng): good find. that explains truncation. will patch normalizer to avoid treating "+" as delimiter.

dion (oncall): closing ops incident once metrics stable for 30m. tagging for follow-up postmortem and RCA.

sara (support): thanks everyone. I'll keep customers updated and attach timeline to the ticket. :white_check_mark:
